messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: Single-solute and mixture experiments use the same soil–CAC system, background electrolyte (1 mM CaCl2 in Milli-Q), L/S = 20, and 14-day equilibration (WEB06-E01, WEB06-E02). These shared conditions reasonably support a status of “comparable_with_conditions” for comparing removal under competition.

The reason cites identical batch conditions (soil type, CAC dose, ionic strength, equilibration time) between single-solute and mixture tests. WEB06-E01 and WEB06-E02 describe one soil, one CAC dose, one background electrolyte condition, and one equilibration time used across experiments, so this inference is supported.
WEB06-E03 and WEB06-E04 report “removal”/“adsorption efficiency” as percent removal of PFAS from solution, which fits the endpoint_type classification as removal.
WEB06-E05 describes distribution coefficients (Kd) and solid–liquid partitioning behavior, which corresponds to a sorption endpoint.

WEB06-E01 states CAC was mixed with a low-organic soil (0.6% organic carbon). WEB06-E02 states solutions were Milli-Q water with 1 mM CaCl2 at L/S = 20 and include seven PFAS, including a seven-compound mixture. Together these support the description of a low-organic soil–water–CAC slurry with the seven PFAS present in mixture tests.
WEB06-E01: “Colloidal activated carbon (PlumeStop, 20% AC, ~900 m²/g, 1–2 µm particles, zeta potential −80 to −2 mV at pH 7)” matches the recorded description.
This field is descriptive (material identity and properties) and correctly leaves unit null; WEB06-E01 supports the qualitative description.
WEB06-E01: CAC was mixed with soil at 0.2% w/w (0.004 g CAC per 2 g soil), matching the recorded dose.
Dose is expressed textually as % w/w and g per g soil within the value string; leaving the structured unit null is acceptable for this qualitative dose description.
WEB06-E02 specifies experiments were conducted at L/S = 20, matching the recorded numeric value 20.
Liquid-to-solid ratio is dimensionless; leaving unit null is appropriate and consistent with WEB06-E02.
WEB06-E02: background solution is “Milli-Q water with 1 mM CaCl2,” so a value of 1 for the concentration is supported.
WEB06-E02 states “1 mM CaCl2,” so the unit mM is correct.
WEB06-E02 reports “14-day equilibration,” supporting the value 14 for equilibration time.
WEB06-E02 uses “14-day equilibration,” so the unit days is correct.

WEB06-E02 gives the overall experimental concentration range (0.002–0.05 mmol/L) but does not specify the exact initial concentration range used specifically for the seven-compound mixture. The record correctly notes the overall range but labels it as the mixture range; thus the core range is supported but its attribution specifically to mixture conditions is only partially supported.
No numeric value is provided and the range is described in the qualifiers; leaving unit null is consistent with the way this field is populated.
WEB06-E02 lists PFPeA among the seven PFAS tested, supporting its inclusion in the PFAS scope for mixture experiments.
WEB06-E02 lists PFHpA among the seven PFAS tested, supporting its inclusion.
WEB06-E02 lists PFNA among the seven PFAS tested, supporting its inclusion.
WEB06-E02 lists PFBS among the seven PFAS tested, supporting its inclusion.
WEB06-E02 lists PFHxS among the seven PFAS tested, supporting its inclusion.
WEB06-E02 lists PFOS among the seven PFAS tested, supporting its inclusion.
WEB06-E02 lists FOSA among the seven PFAS tested, supporting its inclusion.
WEB06-E03: “Average PFAS removal in single-solute systems was 77±7.8%, versus 67±7.1% in the multi-solute mixture.” The value 67 for average mixture removal is correctly transcribed.
Removal is reported in percent in WEB06-E03; unit % is correct.
WEB06-E03 reports the standard deviation for the mixture average removal as 7.1%, correctly captured as 7.1.
The standard deviation is in percentage points; unit % is appropriate and consistent with WEB06-E03.
WEB06-E03 notes that the average removal changes from 77% to 67%, described as a “roughly 10% drop.” Recording an approximate value of ~10 is consistent with this description.
The drop is expressed as a change in percentage removal; unit % is appropriate.
WEB06-E04: “in the mixture removal ranged from 99.8% (FOSA at 0.0003 mmol/L) to 44% (PFOS at 0.007 mmol/L).” The maximum mixture removal of 99.8% is correctly captured.
Removal values in WEB06-E04 are percentages; unit % is correct.
WEB06-E04 states the minimum removal in the mixture is 44% (PFOS at 0.007 mmol/L), matching the recorded value 44.
Removal is reported in percent in WEB06-E04; unit % is correct.

WEB06-E01 and WEB06-E02 show that only one CAC material (PlumeStop), one low-organic soil, and a single CAC dose (0.2% w/w) were used. It is a valid design-inferred limitation that competitive sorption conclusions may not generalize to other adsorbents, soils, or doses.
WEB06-E02 specifies that only seven PFAS (PFPeA, PFHpA, PFNA, PFBS, PFHxS, PFOS, FOSA) were studied. Inferring that other PFAS classes are not represented is a reasonable design-inferred limitation.

WEB06-E03 and WEB06-E05 focus on PFAS removal efficiencies and distribution coefficients without any mention of transformation products or degradation. Inferring that the experiments examine redistribution of parent PFAS only, with no observed byproducts, is reasonable as a design-inferred statement.
WEB06-E01 and WEB06-E02 describe controlled batch sorption experiments using soil–CAC slurries in lab containers (40 mL solutions), which corresponds to bench-scale batch sorption tests.

WEB06-E01 describes PlumeStop colloidal activated carbon (20% AC) mixed with soil at 0.2% w/w. WEB06-E02 indicates these systems treated solutions containing the seven-PFAS mixture. This supports the treatment description.

result.record_usable_rationale: Core elements—source identity, matrix (soil–water–CAC slurry), treatment (PlumeStop CAC at 0.2% w/w), PFAS scope, operating conditions, endpoints (removal and sorption), and quantitative findings for removal—are all directly supported by the cited text with no transcription or unit errors. The only partial issue is attribution of the overall 0.002–0.05 mmol/L range specifically to mixture conditions, which is a minor qualifier issue and does not affect overall usability for synthesis.
